zajjaj:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا جَهَنَّمَ لِلْكافِرِينَ حَصِيرًا﴾ means "a place of confinement (ḥabs)". It is taken from the expression "ḥaṣartu al-rajul" (I confined the man), when you have detained him, so he is "maḥṣūr" (confined); and "hādhā ḥaṣīruhu", i.e. his place of detention. "Al-ḥaṣīr" is also the woven mat; it was only called ḥaṣīr because its strands are pressed together (ḥuṣirat), some with others. And the side of the body is called "al-ḥaṣīr", because some of the ribs are held together (maḥṣūr) with others.

zajjaj:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿إنَّ هَذا القُرْآنَ يَهْدِي لِلَّتِي هي أقْوَمُ﴾, i.e. to the state which is the most upright of states, and that is the affirmation of the Oneness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic — that is, bearing witness that there is no god but Allah — belief in His messengers, and acting in obedience to Him. This is the description of the state which is the most upright of states.

zajjaj:11-11.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَدْعُ الإنْسانُ بِالشَّرِّ دُعاءَهُ بِالخَيْرِ﴾: the meaning is that a person may well, in anger, call down evil upon himself, his child and his family, just as he prays for good for himself; and no human being has been free of this.

It is related «that the Prophet ﷺ handed over a captive to Sawda bint Zamʿa. He began moaning during the night, so she said to him: "What is the matter with you that you are moaning?" He complained of the pain of the fetter and of captivity, so she loosened his bonds. When she fell asleep, he pulled his hand free and fled. When the Prophet ﷺ rose in the morning he called for him, and was told what had happened to him, so he said: "O Allah, cut off her hands." Sawda then raised her hands, expecting the prayer to be answered and that Allah would cut off her hands. So the Prophet ﷺ said: "I have asked Allah to make my prayer and my curse against anyone of my family who does not deserve it a mercy. So tell her: I am a human being; I become angry as human beings become angry. Let Sawda lower her hands."»

So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that man was created hasty; this is what the whole of humankind has been created upon, from Adam to the last of his offspring. "Al-insān" (man) here has the meaning of "al-nās" (people).

zajjaj:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا اللَّيْلَ والنَّهارَ آيَتَيْنِ﴾, i.e. two signs, which indicate that their Creator is One, there being nothing like unto Him, and which indicate the number of years and the reckoning. ﴿فَمَحَوْنا آيَةَ اللَّيْلِ﴾, i.e. We made the sign of the night indicative of it by its darkness. ﴿وَجَعَلْنا آيَةَ النَّهارِ مُبْصِرَةً لِتَبْتَغُوا فَضْلا مِن رَبِّكُمْ﴾, i.e. We made it give you light so that you may see how you go about your work. ﴿وَلِتَعْلَمُوا عَدَدَ السِّنِينَ والحِسابَ﴾. It is related that the moon used to have the brightness of the sun, and Allah effaced its brightness with the darkness that was placed in it.

﴿وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ فَصَّلْناهُ تَفْصِيلا﴾, i.e. We have made it clear with a clarification such that it is not confused with anything else. The preferred reading is the accusative (naṣb) in "كُلَّ". The meaning with the accusative is: "so that you may seek bounty from your Lord, and so that you may know the number of the years, and We have set out everything in detail (wa-faṣṣalnā kulla shayʾin tafṣīlan)". "كُلَّ" is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmar) verb, which the overt one — "فَصَّلْناهُ" — explains. It is also permissible to say "وَكُلُّ شَيْءٍ فَصَّلْناهُ تَفْصِيلًا" (in the nominative). Likewise the accusative and the nominative are both possible in His saying: ﴿وَكُلَّ إنْسانٍ ألْزَمْناهُ طائِرَهُ في عُنُقِهِ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 13], except that I know of no one who read it in the nominative.

It has come in the exegesis that "طائِرُهُ" (his omen) means "his good and his evil", and it is — and Allah knows best — whatever deed of his of the kind from which one draws an ill omen, as He said: ﴿لِيَحْمِلُوا أوْزارَهم كامِلَةً يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 25], and as one says to a person: "my sin is on your neck". Something that clings to a person is spoken of as "this is on the person's neck", i.e. it clings to him as the necklace clings to him, among the things worn on the neck. ﴿وَنُخْرِجُ لَهُ يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ كِتابًا يَلْقاهُ مَنشُورًا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 13]: in this there are four possibilities: "وَتُخْرَجُ لَهُ" (and it will be brought out for him); "وَيُخْرِجُ لَهُ", i.e. "and Allah will bring out for him"; "وَيَخْرُجُ لَهُ", i.e. "and his deed will come out for him on the Day of Resurrection as a book"; and likewise "يُخْرَجُ لَهُ عَمَلُهُ يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ" (his deed will be brought out for him on the Day of Resurrection). ﴿كِتابًا يَلْقاهُ مَنشُورًا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 13] is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

zajjaj:14-14.t: His saying: ﴿كَفى بِنَفْسِكَ اليَوْمَ عَلَيْكَ حَسِيبًا﴾: "بِنَفْسِكَ" is in the position of the nominative (rafʿ), even though it is made genitive by the bāʾ. Were it not in the Qurʾān, "كَفى بِنَفْسِكَ اليَوْمَ حَسِيبَةً" (with the feminine) would be permissible. The meaning is: "your self suffices as a reckoner", i.e. "since you bear witness against yourself, this is sufficient for you". "حَسِيبًا" is accusative as a tamyīz (specification).

zajjaj:15-15.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلا تَزِرُ وازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرى﴾: one says "wazara, yaziru" — so he is "wāzir" — with the verbal nouns "wazran", "wizran" and "zira", and its meaning is "athima, yaʾthamu, ithman" (to sin). There are two interpretations of this verse. One of them is that the sinner and the wrongdoer — no one else is taken to account for his sin. The second interpretation is that a person ought not to commit sin because someone else committed it, as the disbelievers said: ﴿إنّا وجَدْنا آباءَنا عَلى أُمَّةٍ وإنّا عَلى آثارِهِمْ مُهْتَدُونَ﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 22].

His saying: ﴿وَما كُنّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتّى نَبْعَثَ رَسُولا﴾, i.e. until We make clear that for which We punish, and that on account of which We admit to Paradise.

zajjaj:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإذا أرَدْنا أنْ نُهْلِكَ قَرْيَةً أمَرْنا مُتْرَفِيها فَفَسَقُوا فِيها﴾: it is read "أمَرْنا", without doubling, on the pattern of "faʿalnā"; it is read "آمَرْنا مُتْرَفِيها", on the pattern of "afʿalnā"; and it is read "أمَّرْنا", with the mīm doubled. As for whoever read it without doubling, it is from "al-amr" (command); the meaning is: "We commanded them to obey, but they acted sinfully."

If someone were to say: do you not say "I commanded Zayd and he struck ʿAmr", the meaning being that you commanded him to strike ʿAmr and he struck him, so that this wording indicates nothing other than the striking? [The answer is that] the equivalent of His saying ﴿أمَرْنا مُتْرَفِيها فَفَسَقُوا فِيها﴾ in ordinary speech is "I commanded you, and you disobeyed me": it is known that disobedience is contrary to the command, and likewise sinfulness (fisq) is contrary to the command of Allah, exalted be His praise. [Translator's note: the bracketed words "The answer is that" are added for clarity; the Arabic moves straight from the objection to the reply.]

It has also been said that the meaning of "أمَرْنا مُتْرَفِيها" is only "We multiplied its affluent ones", and the evidence for this is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: «"The best of wealth is a row of pollinated palms and a prolific (maʾmūra) filly"», i.e. one made to multiply. The Arabs say "qad amira banū fulān" (the sons of so-and-so have amira) when they have become numerous. The poet said:
؎إنْ يُغْبَطُوا يَهْبِطُوا وإنْ أمِرُوا يَوْمًا يَصِيرُوا لِلْهَلْكِ والنَّفَدِ
(If they are envied [for their prosperity] they decline, and if one day they grow numerous, they come to destruction and depletion.)
It is also narrated as "bi-l-naqd", with qāf.

Whoever read "آمَرْنا", its interpretation is "We made numerous", and the abundance here may be one of two things: one of them is that the number of the affluent increases, and the other is that their wealth and riches increase. Whoever read "أمَّرْنا", with doubling, its meaning is "We gave its affluent ones authority", i.e. We granted them rule and power.

zajjaj:17-17.t: His saying: ﴿وَكَمْ أهْلَكْنا مِنَ القُرُونِ مِن بَعْدِ نُوحٍ﴾, i.e. We destroyed a great number of generations with various kinds of punishment, such as the people of Lūṭ, ʿĀd, Thamūd, and those whose names have been mentioned, ﴿وَقُرُونًا بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ كَثِيرًا﴾ [al-Furqān: 38]. The position of "كَمْ" is the accusative, by His saying "أهْلَكْنا".

zajjaj:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿مَن كانَ يُرِيدُ العاجِلَةَ عَجَّلْنا لَهُ فِيها ما نَشاءُ لِمَن نُرِيدُ﴾, i.e. whoever by his deeds desires the hasty [world] — that is, this world — Allah hastens to whomever He wishes to hasten it for whatever Allah wills, i.e. not what he himself wills. "Mā yashāʾu" (what He wills) has the meaning of "ما نَشاءُ" (what We will). It is also possible that the implied pronoun in "نَشاءُ" refers to "مَن" (whoever); the meaning would then be: "We hasten for the servant what he desires", if Allah wills that. [Translator's note: the text says the implied pronoun in "نشاء" could refer to "من", although "نشاء" is first-person plural; this is translated as written.]

His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ جَعَلْنا لَهُ جَهَنَّمَ﴾ — because he did not seek Allah by his deeds — ﴿يَصْلاها مَذْمُومًا﴾; "madhmūm" and "madhʾūm" (blamed, disgraced) have one meaning. ﴿مَدْحُورًا﴾, i.e. driven far from the mercy of Allah. One says "daḥartuhu, adḥaruhu, daḥran, wa-duḥūran" when you have driven him far away from you. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that He gives to both the Muslim and the disbeliever and provides for them both, so He said: ﴿كُلا نُمِدُّ هَؤُلاءِ وهَؤُلاءِ مِن عَطاءِ رَبِّكَ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 20], i.e. We supply the believers and the disbelievers from the bounty of your Lord.

zajjaj:23-23.t:
His saying, glorified is He: ﴿وَقَضى رَبُّكَ ألا تَعْبُدُوا إلا إيّاهُ﴾ — its meaning is "your Lord has commanded".

﴿وَبِالوالِدَيْنِ إحْسانًا﴾, i.e. He commanded that they do good to the parents. ﴿إمّا يَبْلُغَنَّ عِنْدَكَ الكِبَرَ أحَدُهُما أوْ كِلاهُما﴾: "أحَدُهُما" is made nominative by "يَبْلُغَنَّ" [as its fāʿil (agent)], and "كِلاهُما" is conjoined to it. It is also read "يَبْلُغانِّ عِنْدَكَ الكِبَرَ", in which case "أحَدُهُما أوْ كِلاهُما" is a badal (substitute) for the alif [of the dual]. [Translator's note: the bracketed words are added for clarity.]

His saying: ﴿فَلا تَقُلْ لَهُما أُفٍّ﴾: in His word "أُفٍّ" there are seven dialectal forms: the kasra without tanwīn (nunation), the kasra with tanwīn, the ḍamma without tanwīn and with tanwīn, and likewise the fatḥa with tanwīn and without tanwīn; and there is another, seventh form in which it is not permissible to recite, namely "أُفِّي", with yāʾ. As for the kasra, it is because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. "أُفٍّ" is not fully declinable (ghayr mutamakkin); it is like the sound-words (al-aṣwāt): when it is not nunated it is definite, and when it is nunated it is indefinite, like "ghāqin" and "ghāqi" among the sound-words. The fatḥa is likewise because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the fatḥa together with the doubling is good, because of the lightness of the fatḥa and the heaviness of the doubling. The ḍamma, because what precedes it has a ḍamma, is also good. The tanwīn in all of it is by way of indefiniteness.

The meaning is: "do not say to them words in which you show your irritation with them". The meaning of "أُفِّ" is a foul smell; it has also been said that "uffa" is the dirt under the nails, and "al-tuff" is something worthless, like the dirt of the ears, or a splinter picked up from the ground. The meaning of the verse is: "do not say to them anything hurtful out of irritation", i.e. when they have grown old or advanced in years, you should take upon yourself serving them as they took upon themselves looking after your affairs and serving you. ﴿وَلا تَنْهَرْهُما﴾ means "do not rebuke them (lā tantahirhumā)", i.e. do not speak to them in annoyance, shouting in their faces. One says "nahartuhu, anharuhu, nahran" and "intahartuhu, antahiruhu, intihāran" with one meaning.

zajjaj:24-24.t: His saying: ﴿واخْفِضْ لَهُما جَناحَ الذُّلِّ مِنَ الرَّحْمَةِ﴾ — it is also read "اَلذِّلِّ", with kasra on the dhāl. The meaning of "lower to them the wing of humility" is: make yourself gentle towards them, humbling yourself before them, out of your utmost mercy towards them. One says "rajulun dhalīl" (a lowly man), plain in his dhull (lowliness), and "qad dhalla, yadhillu, dhullan"; and "dābbatun dhalūl" (a docile mount), plain in its dhill (docility); and both are permissible of a human being.

zajjaj:25-25.t: His saying: ﴿فَإنَّهُ كانَ لِلأوّابِينَ غَفُورًا﴾: "al-awwāb" has the meaning of "al-tawwāb" (the one who repents often), and "the one who returns to Allah in everything He has commanded and desists from everything He has forbidden". One says "qad āba, yaʾūbu, awban" when he has returned.

zajjaj:26-26.t: His saying: ﴿وَلا تُبَذِّرْ تَبْذِيرًا﴾ means: do not be extravagant. It has been said: al-tabdhīr (squandering) is spending in other than obedience to Allah. It has also been said: the people of the Jāhiliyya used to slaughter camels and squander wealth, seeking thereby pride and renown, and they would mention that in their poetry; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded spending in its proper ways, on what brings one near to Him and gains closeness with Him.

zajjaj:27-27.t: His saying: ﴿إنَّ المُبَذِّرِينَ كانُوا إخْوانَ الشَّياطِينِ﴾, i.e. they do what Satan makes seem fair to them.

zajjaj:28-28.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإمّا تُعْرِضَنَّ عَنْهُمُ ابْتِغاءَ رَحْمَةٍ مِن رَبِّكَ تَرْجُوها﴾: in "عَنْهُمْ", the hāʾ and the mīm refer back to the near relative, the needy and the wayfarer. "وَإمّا تُعْرِضَنَّ عَنْهُمْ" means "and if you turn away from them". ﴿ابْتِغاءَ رَحْمَةٍ مِن رَبِّكَ تَرْجُوها﴾, i.e. in seeking provision from your Lord which you hope for. ﴿فَقُلْ لَهم قَوْلا مَيْسُورًا﴾. "اِبْتِغاءَ" is accusative because it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); the meaning is: "and if you turn away from them in seeking mercy from your Lord".

It is related «that when the Prophet ﷺ was asked for something and had nothing to give, he would hold back, waiting for provision to come from Allah, Majestic and Mighty, as though he disliked refusing. When this verse was revealed — ﴿فَقُلْ لَهم قَوْلا مَيْسُورًا﴾ — whenever he, upon him be peace, was asked and had nothing to give, he would say: "May Allah provide for us and for you from His bounty."» So the interpretation of His word ﴿مَيْسُورًا﴾ — and Allah knows best — is that he would soften the blow of their poverty for them by his prayer for them.

zajjaj:29-29.t: His saying: ﴿وَلا تَجْعَلْ يَدَكَ مَغْلُولَةً إلى عُنُقِكَ ولا تَبْسُطْها كُلَّ البَسْطِ﴾ means: do not be miserly and do not be extravagant. "فَتَقْعُدَ" is accusative as the answer to the prohibition. "مَحْسُورًا" means: "you have overburdened yourself and your circumstances until you become like one who is utterly exhausted". "Al-ḥasīr" and "al-maḥsūr" mean one who has reached the limit of fatigue and exhaustion.

zajjaj:31-31.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلا تَقْتُلُوا أوْلادَكم خَشْيَةَ إمْلاقٍ﴾: "خَشْيَةَ إمْلاقٍ" is accusative because it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). "Al-imlāq" is poverty; one says "amlaqa, yamliqu, imlāqan". [Translator's note: the source has "يَمْلُقُ" as the imperfect, as printed.] They used to bury daughters when they were born to them, out of fear of poverty, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, guaranteed them their provision and said: ﴿نَحْنُ نَرْزُقُهم وإيّاكُمْ﴾. This is the mawʾūda (the girl buried alive): they used to bury the daughter alive when she was born.

His saying: ﴿إنَّ قَتْلَهم كانَ خِطْئًا كَبِيرًا﴾ — it is also read "خَطَأً كَبِيرًا". Whoever says "خِطْئًا", with kasra, its meaning is a great sin; one says "qad khaṭiʾa al-rajulu, yakhṭaʾu, khiṭʾan", i.e. "athima, yaʾthamu, ithman" (he sinned). "خَطَأً كَبِيرًا" has two interpretations. One of them means: "their killing was not right"; one says "qad akhṭaʾa, yukhṭiʾu, ikhṭāʾan wa-khaṭaʾan", and "al-khaṭaʾ" is the noun from this, not the maṣdar (verbal noun). And "al-khaṭaʾ" may be from "khaṭiʾa, yakhṭaʾu, khaṭaʾan" when he fails to hit the mark, like "lajija, yalijju". [Translator's note: the source writes this example as "لَجَجَ، يَلْجَجُ".] The poet said:
؎والنّاسُ يَلْحَوْنَ الأمِيرَ إذا هُمُ خَطِئُوا الصَّوابَ ولا يُلامُ المُرْشِدُ
(People blame the commander when they themselves miss what is right, while the one who guides aright is not blamed.)

zajjaj:32-32.t: His saying: ﴿وَساءَ سَبِيلا﴾, i.e. "and evil is fornication as a way". "سَبِيلًا" is accusative as a tamyīz (specification).

zajjaj:33-33.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلا تَقْتُلُوا النَّفْسَ الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ إلا بِالحَقِّ﴾: Allah has forbidden the killing of a believer, unless he apostatises after his faith, or kills a believer deliberately, or commits fornication after iḥṣān (being married); this is what Qatāda said in the interpretation of this verse. ﴿وَمَن قُتِلَ مَظْلُومًا﴾, i.e. without having committed one of these three. ﴿فَقَدْ جَعَلْنا لِوَلِيِّهِ سُلْطانًا﴾: the best is to assimilate the dāl into the jīm, and pronouncing it distinctly (iẓhār) is good and excellent, because the jīm is from the middle of the tongue and the dāl from the tip of the tongue; assimilation is permissible because the letters of the middle of the tongue may come close to the letters of the tip of the tongue. His walī (next of kin) is the one who has with him a kinship that entitles him to demand his blood; if he has no walī, then the ruler (al-sulṭān) is his walī. "سُلْطانًا" means "a proof (ḥujja)".

His saying: ﴿فَلا يُسْرِفْ في القَتْلِ﴾: the reading is the jussive (jazm), as a prohibition, and it is read with both yāʾ and tāʾ; it is also read "فَلا يُسْرِفُ", in the nominative. There is disagreement about excess in killing. Most people said: "excess" is that the walī kills someone other than the killer of his kinsman. It has also been said: "excess" is that he himself kills the killer without [recourse to] the ruler. When a chief among the Arabs was killed, and his killer was of low standing, they would not be content with the killing of his killer; and sometimes they would not be content with one being killed for one, until a group was killed for one.

His saying: ﴿إنَّهُ كانَ مَنصُورًا﴾, i.e. the slain person, when he is killed without right, is helped in this world and the Hereafter. As for his being helped in this world, it is the killing of his killer; as for the Hereafter, it is the abundance of reward for him, while his killer abides forever in the Fire. Whoever reads "فَلا يُسْرِفُ في القَتْلِ", in the nominative, the meaning is that his walī is not excessive in killing when he kills his killer and does not accept the blood-money.

zajjaj:34-34.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلا تَقْرَبُوا مالَ اليَتِيمِ إلا بِالَّتِي هي أحْسَنُ حَتّى يَبْلُغَ أشُدَّهُ﴾, i.e. do not store away any of his wealth, and when you are put in charge of him, do not eat [of it] except what stills hunger, and do not clothe yourselves except with what covers the ʿawra (the private parts), and do not approach it except to put the wealth in good order. ﴿حَتّى يَبْلُغَ أشُدَّهُ﴾: his ashudd (full strength) is that he reaches the age of marriage. It has also been said: his ashudd is that he reaches eighteen years. Reaching his ashudd is sexual maturity, together with his being free of any defect of mind and being prudent with his wealth.

His saying: ﴿وَأوْفُوا بِالعَهْدِ إنَّ العَهْدَ كانَ مَسْؤُولا﴾: one of them said: "I do not know what the covenant is." "Al-ʿahd" (the covenant) is everything one has pledged to Allah, and all the agreements between the servants are covenants; likewise His saying: ﴿وَأوْفُوا بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ إذا عاهَدْتُمْ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 91].

zajjaj:35-35.t:
His saying: ﴿وَزِنُوا بِالقِسْطاسِ المُسْتَقِيمِ﴾ — "al-qusṭās" too, i.e. with both ḍamma and kasra. It has been said: "al-qisṭās" is "al-qurusṭūn" (the steelyard); it has also been said: "al-qaffān" (the balance-beam); and "al-qisṭās" is the scale of justice, whatever scale it may be, among the scales for dirhams or others.

His saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ خَيْرٌ وأحْسَنُ تَأْوِيلا﴾: the meaning of "and better in outcome (aḥsanu taʾwīlan)" is that giving full measure is better than giving short. It is also possible that the meaning is: "the best of what the affair of the one who gives full measure comes to (yaʾūlu ilayhi)".

zajjaj:36-36.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلا تَقْفُ ما لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ﴾, i.e. "do not say about anything what you do not know". If the Prophet ﷺ, with his wisdom, his knowledge and Allah's granting him success, was forbidden to say what he does not know, then how much more the rest of his community, and those who have transgressed against themselves?! One says "qafawtu al-shayʾa, aqfūhu, qafwan" when you follow its trace. So the interpretation is: "do not let your tongue follow, in speech, that of which you have no knowledge", and likewise for all of the mind. ﴿إنَّ السَّمْعَ والبَصَرَ والفُؤادَ﴾ are witnesses against you. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿يَوْمَ تَشْهَدُ عَلَيْهِمْ ألْسِنَتُهم وأيْدِيهِمْ وأرْجُلُهم بِما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ [al-Nūr: 24]; so the limbs are witnesses against the son of Adam concerning his deeds. It is also read "وَلا تَقُفْ ما لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ", with sukūn on the fāʾ and ḍamma on the qāf, from "qāfa, yaqūfu"; it seems to be a metathesis (maqlūb) of "qafā, yaqfū", because the meaning is the same.

His saying: ﴿كُلُّ أُولَئِكَ كانَ عَنْهُ مَسْؤُولا﴾: He said "مَسْؤُولًا" and He said "كانَ" [in the singular] because "كُلُّ" is singular in form. And He said "أُولَئِكَ" for other than people, because every plural you point to, whether of people or others, or of inanimate things, has the form "أُولَئِكَ". Jarīr said:
؎ذُمَّ المَنازِلَ بَعْدَ مَنزِلَةِ اللِّوى والعَيْشَ بَعْدَ أُولَئِكَ الأيّامِ
(Find fault with every dwelling after the dwelling at al-Liwā, and with life after those days.)

zajjaj:37-37.t: His saying: ﴿وَلا تَمْشِ في الأرْضِ مَرَحًا﴾ — it is also read "مَرِحًا", with kasra on the rāʾ. Al-Akhfash claimed that "مَرَحًا" is better than "مَرِحًا", because "مَرِحًا" is the active participle. This — I mean the maṣdar (verbal noun) — is good and excellent, and both are equal in quality, except that the maṣdar is more emphatic in usage. You say "jāʾa Zaydun rakḍan" (Zayd came at a gallop) and "jāʾa Zaydun rākiḍan" (Zayd came galloping); "rakḍan" is more emphatic in usage, because "rakḍan" indicates emphasis of the verb. "مَرَحًا", with fatḥa on the rāʾ, is more common in recitation. The interpretation of the verse is: "do not walk on the earth conceitedly and boastfully". ﴿إنَّكَ لَنْ تَخْرِقَ الأرْضَ ولَنْ تَبْلُغَ الجِبالَ طُولا﴾: they said that the meaning of "you will not rend the earth" is "you will not traverse the earth"; it has also been said: "you will not pierce the earth". The interpretation is that your power does not reach this extent, such that it might be a means to arrogance.

zajjaj:38-38.t: ﴿كُلُّ ذَلِكَ كانَ سَيِّئُهُ عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ مَكْرُوهًا﴾: "سَيِّئُهُ" is in the meaning of "a sin (khaṭīʾa)". Abū ʿAmr would not read "سَيِّئُهُ" but read "سَيِّئَةً", and this is a mistake, because in the narrated commands there is what is evil and what is not evil. That is because among them is: ﴿وَقُلْ لَهُما قَوْلا كَرِيمًا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 23] ﴿واخْفِضْ لَهُما جَناحَ الذُّلِّ مِنَ الرَّحْمَةِ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 24], and among them: ﴿وَآتِ ذا القُرْبى حَقَّهُ والمِسْكِينَ وابْنَ السَّبِيلِ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 26], and ﴿وَأوْفُوا بِالعَهْدِ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 34], ﴿وَلا تَقْرَبُوا مالَ اليَتِيمِ إلا بِالَّتِي هي أحْسَنُ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 34], i.e. approach it with that which is best. So in the verses that have passed there is the evil and the good, and therefore "سَيِّئُهُ", without tanwīn, is better than "سَيِّئَةً" here. Whoever read "سَيِّئَةً" made "كُلُّ" encompass only what is forbidden; the meaning is: "everything Allah has forbidden was an evil deed".

zajjaj:39-39.t: His saying: ﴿فَتُلْقى في جَهَنَّمَ مَلُومًا مَدْحُورًا﴾, i.e. driven far from the mercy of Allah.

zajjaj:40-40.t: His saying: ﴿أفَأصْفاكم رَبُّكم بِالبَنِينَ﴾: the disbelievers among the Arabs used to claim that the angels were the daughters of Allah, so they were rebuked, and it was said to them: ﴿أفَأصْفاكم رَبُّكم بِالبَنِينَ﴾, i.e. "Has your Lord chosen for you the choicest of things, and taken from the angels what is not the choicest?!"

zajjaj:41-41.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْنا في هَذا القُرْآنِ لِيَذَّكَّرُوا﴾, i.e. We have made clear. ﴿وَما يَزِيدُهم إلا نُفُورًا﴾, i.e. the clarification increases them only in aversion, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَنُنَـزِّلُ مِنَ القُرْآنِ ما هو شِفاءٌ ورَحْمَةٌ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ ولا يَزِيدُ الظّالِمِينَ إلا خَسارًا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 82].

zajjaj:42-42.t: ﴿قُلْ لَوْ كانَ مَعَهُ آلِهَةٌ كَما يَقُولُونَ﴾ — whoever read "كَما تَقُولُونَ" (as you say), it is by way of addressing those who say it. ﴿إذًا لابْتَغَوْا إلى ذِي العَرْشِ سَبِيلا﴾, i.e. they would have sought nearness to the Lord of the Throne, as He said: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ يَبْتَغُونَ إلى رَبِّهِمُ الوَسِيلَةَ أيُّهم أقْرَبُ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 57]. Some of them said: "إذًا لابْتَغَوْا إلى ذِي العَرْشِ سَبِيلًا" means they would have been opposed to Him, seeking to be alone in lordship. The first view is the one held by the exegetes.

zajjaj:44-44.t: His saying: ﴿تُسَبِّحُ لَهُ السَّماواتُ السَّبْعُ والأرْضُ ومَن فِيهِنَّ وإنْ مِن شَيْءٍ إلا يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِهِ ولَكِنْ لا تَفْقَهُونَ تَسْبِيحَهُمْ﴾: it has been said that everything Allah has created glorifies Him with His praise, and that the creaking of the roof and the creaking of the door are part of the glorification of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. On this view, the address in His saying ﴿وَلَكِنْ لا تَفْقَهُونَ تَسْبِيحَهُمْ﴾ is to the idolaters alone. It is also possible that the glorification of these things is among what Allah knows, and none of it is understood except what He has taught us. Some people said: "وَإنْ مِن شَيْءٍ إلّا يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِهِ" means "there is nothing but that in it there is evidence that Allah is its Creator, and that its Creator is Wise, free of all evils; but you do not understand their glorification — i.e. but you, O disbelievers, do not understand the trace of the craftsmanship in these created things". This is worth nothing, because those who were addressed by this acknowledged that Allah was their Creator and the Creator of the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them; so how could they be ignorant of the creation when they knew it?!

zajjaj:45-45.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإذا قَرَأْتَ القُرْآنَ جَعَلْنا بَيْنَكَ وبَيْنَ الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالآخِرَةِ حِجابًا مَسْتُورًا﴾: the lexicographers said that the meaning of "مَسْتُورًا" (veiled) here is in the place of "sātiran" (veiling). The interpretation of the veil — and Allah knows best — is the seal that is upon their hearts, and what indicates that is His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلْنا عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ أكِنَّةً أنْ يَفْقَهُوهُ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 46]. "Al-akinna" is the plural of "kinān", which is whatever covers. The meaning of "أنْ يَفْقَهُوهُ" is "out of aversion that they should understand it"; it has also been said that its meaning is "so that they do not understand it". The two meanings are one, except that "aversion (karāhata)" is better in Arabic. It has also been said about ﴿جَعَلْنا بَيْنَكَ وبَيْنَ الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالآخِرَةِ حِجابًا مَسْتُورًا﴾ that "the veil" is Allah's preventing them from [reaching] the Prophet, upon him be peace. It is also possible that "مَسْتُورًا" is not in the meaning of "sātiran", so that the veil is something they neither see nor know, namely the seal upon their hearts.

﴿وَفِي آذانِهِمْ وقْرًا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 46]: "al-waqr" is heaviness of hearing; and "al-wiqr" is that a person carries his load. [Translator's note: the printed text vocalises both words as "اَلْوَقْرُ"; the second is presumably "al-wiqr" (a load).]

His saying: ﴿وَلَّوْا عَلى أدْبارِهِمْ نُفُورًا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 46]: "نُفُورًا" admits two analyses. One of them is the maṣdar (verbal noun); the meaning is "they turned away, fleeing in aversion (nāfirīna nufūran)". It is also possible that "نُفُورًا" is the plural of "nāfir", so that "nāfir" and "nufūr" are like "shāhid" and "shuhūd".

zajjaj:47-47.t:
His saying: ﴿إذْ يَسْتَمِعُونَ إلَيْكَ وإذْ هم نَجْوى﴾: "نَجْوى" is in the meaning of the maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "and when they are people of secret counsel"; "al-najwā" is a noun standing for the maṣdar. They used to listen to the Prophet ﷺ and say among themselves: "He is a sorcerer", "he is bewitched", and words of that sort. The lexicographers gave two views on His saying ﴿إلا رَجُلا مَسْحُورًا﴾. One of them is that "مَسْحُورًا" means one having a saḥr, and "al-saḥr" is the lung [lit. "al-ranna"]; and they said: "you are only following one who has a lung — a human being like you, who eats food". [Translator's note: the source has "اَلرَّنَّةُ" here, as printed; the usual explanation of saḥr in this context is "al-riʾa" (the lung), i.e. a mortal who breathes and eats.] Labīd said:
؎فَإنْ تَسْألِينا فِيمَ نَحْنُ فَإنَّنا عَصافِيرُ مِن هَذا الأنامِ المُسَحَّرِ
(If you ask us what we are, we are but sparrows of this mankind that is given lungs [and is fed].)
And they said that "مَسْحُورًا" means: one who has been bewitched and removed from the bounds of soundness.

zajjaj:49-49.t:
﴿وَقالُوا أإذا كُنّا عِظامًا ورُفاتًا أإنّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ خَلْقًا جَدِيدًا﴾: "al-rufāt" is dust; and "al-rufāt" is also anything that has been crushed and broken. Everything of this kind is built on the pattern "fuʿāl", such as "al-futāt" (crumbs), "al-ḥuṭām" (debris), "al-rufāt" and "al-turāb" (dust).

His saying: ﴿خَلْقًا جَدِيدًا﴾ is in the meaning of "renewed".

zajjaj:50-50.t:
His saying: ﴿قُلْ كُونُوا حِجارَةً أوْ حَدِيدًا﴾ ﴿أوْ خَلْقًا مِمّا يَكْبُرُ في صُدُورِكُمْ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 51]: most of what has come in the exegesis of His saying ﴿أوْ خَلْقًا مِمّا يَكْبُرُ في صُدُورِكُمْ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 51] is that this creation is death. It has also been said that "a creation of what is great in your breasts" is something like the heavens, the earth and the mountains. The meaning of this verse has a subtlety and an obscurity in it, because someone may say: how can it be said to them "be stones or iron", when they are not able to do that?!

The answer to that is that they used to acknowledge that Allah, exalted be His praise, was their Creator, yet they denied that Allah would bring them back as another creation. So it was said to them: realise that even if you had been created of stone or iron, Allah would cause you to die and then bring you to life, because the power by which He brought you into being — and you acknowledge that He brought you into being by that power — is the power by which He will bring you back, even if you were stones or iron, or you were death itself, which is the greatest of things in your breasts.

His saying: ﴿فَسَيَقُولُونَ مَن يُعِيدُنا قُلِ الَّذِي فَطَرَكم أوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ فَسَيُنْغِضُونَ إلَيْكَ رُءُوسَهُمْ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 51], i.e. they will shake their heads, as one shakes it who considers a thing false and thinks it far off. ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ مَتى هُوَ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 51]. One says "anghaḍtu raʾsī — when I have shaken it — unghiḍuhu, inghāḍan"; and "naghaḍat al-sinnu, tanghaḍu, naghḍan" (the tooth became loose); and "naghaḍa bi-raʾsihi, yunghiḍu, naghḍan" when he shakes it. [Translator's note: the source gives the imperfect "يُنْغِضُ" here with the first-form maṣdar "نَغْضًا", as printed.] Al-ʿAjjāj said:
؎أسَكَّ نَغْضًا لا يَنِي مُسْتَهْدَجا
(An earless one [i.e. an ostrich], bobbing [its head], never ceasing to hurry along in haste.)

zajjaj:52-52.t: His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ يَدْعُوكم فَتَسْتَجِيبُونَ بِحَمْدِهِ﴾, i.e. He will bring you back on the Day of Resurrection. The meaning of "you will respond with His praise" is: "you will respond acknowledging that He is your Creator".

zajjaj:55-55.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ فَضَّلْنا بَعْضَ النَّبِيِّينَ عَلى بَعْضٍ وآتَيْنا داوُدَ زَبُورًا﴾: the significance of mentioning Dāwūd here is that Allah, exalted be His praise, made known that He has preferred some prophets over others; i.e. so let them not deny the preference of Muḥammad ﷺ and His giving him the Qurʾān, for Allah gave Dāwūd the Psalms (al-Zabūr).

zajjaj:56-56.t: His saying: ﴿قُلِ ادْعُوا الَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُمْ مِن دُونِهِ فَلا يَمْلِكُونَ كَشْفَ الضُّرِّ عَنْكم ولا تَحْوِيلا﴾, i.e. call upon those whom you claimed to be your gods. Several things have come in the exegesis concerning this verse. Among them is that it was said: "Say: call upon ʿUzayr and ʿĪsā", because the Christians and the Jews claimed that these were their gods; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known to them that they have no power to remove harm from them, nor to shift it from one to another. It has also been said that the angels are meant by it, because among them were some who worshipped the angels. It has also been said that some people of the Arabs used to worship a band of the jinn; then that band of the jinn embraced Islam, without those who worshipped them knowing of it, so it was said: "Then call upon these, for they possess neither harm nor benefit."

zajjaj:57-57.t:
His saying: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ يَبْتَغُونَ إلى رَبِّهِمُ الوَسِيلَةَ﴾ — with yāʾ and with tāʾ [i.e. "yadʿūna" and "tadʿūna"]. "أُولَئِكَ" is nominative as the mubtadaʾ (subject); "اَلَّذِينَ" is nominative as an adjective (ṣifa) for them; and "يَبْتَغُونَ" is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. The meaning is: "the group whom they call upon themselves seek a means of approach to their Lord". "Al-wasīla" (means of approach), "al-suʾāl", "al-suʾl" and "al-ṭilba" (request) have one meaning. ﴿أيُّهم أقْرَبُ﴾: if you wish, "أيُّهُمْ" is nominative as the mubtadaʾ and the khabar is "أقْرَبُ", and the meaning would be: "they seek a means of approach to their Lord, looking to see which of them is nearest to Him, so that they may seek approach through him".

If someone says: then what was condemned in them was seeking approach to Allah through something other than the worship of Allah, because they said: ﴿ما نَعْبُدُهم إلا لِيُقَرِّبُونا إلى اللَّهِ زُلْفى﴾ [al-Zumar: 3] — [the answer is that] the difference [between them and] those who seek approach to Allah through love of His prophets, His angels and His righteous servants is that the latter seek approach through them while affirming the Oneness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, not making for Him any partner in worship, whereas the disbelievers seek approach by worshipping other than Allah, so they made disbelief their means of approach. [Translator's note: the bracketed words are added for clarity.]

It is also possible that "أيُّهم أقْرَبُ" is a badal (substitute) for the wāw in "يَبْتَغُونَ"; the meaning then is: "whichever of them is nearest seeks the means of approach to Allah", i.e. draws near to Him through righteous deeds. ﴿وَيَرْجُونَ رَحْمَتَهُ ويَخافُونَ عَذابَهُ﴾, i.e. "those whom they claim to be gods [themselves] hope and fear".

zajjaj:58-58.t: His saying: ﴿وَإنْ مِن قَرْيَةٍ إلا نَحْنُ مُهْلِكُوها قَبْلَ يَوْمِ القِيامَةِ﴾, i.e. "there are no people of a town but that they will perish, either by death or by a punishment that uproots them". ﴿كانَ ذَلِكَ في الكِتابِ مَسْطُورًا﴾, i.e. written.

zajjaj:59-59.t: ﴿وَما مَنَعَنا أنْ نُرْسِلَ بِالآياتِ إلا أنْ كَذَّبَ بِها الأوَّلُونَ﴾: the first "أنْ" is in the accusative and the second "أنْ" is in the nominative; the meaning is: "nothing prevented Us from sending except the denial of the former peoples". The interpretation is that they asked for the signs by which the former peoples had incurred punishment when they denied them, so that the punishment came down upon them. The evidence that they asked for those signs is their saying: ﴿لَوْلا أُوتِيَ مِثْلَ ما أُوتِيَ مُوسى﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 48]. So Allah, exalted be His praise, made known that the appointed time of the disbelievers of this community is the Hour, and said: ﴿بَلِ السّاعَةُ مَوْعِدُهم والسّاعَةُ أدْهى وأمَرُّ﴾ [al-Qamar: 46]; so He deferred them until the Day of Resurrection, out of mercy and grace from Him. ﴿وَآتَيْنا ثَمُودَ النّاقَةَ مُبْصِرَةً﴾ — it is also read "مُبْصَرَةً". Whoever read "مُبْصِرَةً", the meaning is: it gives them insight, i.e. makes things clear to them; and whoever read "مُبْصَرَةً", the meaning is: made clear. ﴿فَظَلَمُوا بِها﴾, i.e. they did wrong by denying it.

zajjaj:60-60.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإذْ قُلْنا لَكَ إنَّ رَبَّكَ أحاطَ بِالنّاسِ﴾: it has come in the exegesis that "He encompasses them" means all of them are in His grasp. And from al-Ḥasan: "He encompasses the people" means He came between them and their killing you or overpowering you, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿واللَّهُ يَعْصِمُكَ مِنَ النّاسِ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 67].

His saying: ﴿وَما جَعَلْنا الرُّؤْيا الَّتِي أرَيْناكَ إلا فِتْنَةً لِلنّاسِ﴾: it has come in the exegesis that it is the vision of Bayt al-Maqdis when he was taken by night. That is because some of them apostatised when he informed them of the story of his Night Journey, while the sincere believers increased in faith. It has also come in the exegesis «that he ﷺ saw in his sleep a people mounting the pulpits, and that grieved him; then he ﷺ was told that it was a gift in this world».

﴿والشَّجَرَةَ المَلْعُونَةَ في القُرْآنِ﴾: it was said in the exegesis: "the one whose eating is cursed", and it is the tree of al-Zaqqūm which Allah mentioned in the Qurʾān, saying: ﴿إنَّ شَجَرَتَ الزَّقُّومِ﴾ [al-Dukhān: 43] ﴿طَعامُ الأثِيمِ﴾ [al-Dukhān: 44], and He said: ﴿فَإنَّهم لآكِلُونَ مِنها فَمالِئُونَ مِنها البُطُونَ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 66], and He said: ﴿إنَّها شَجَرَةٌ تَخْرُجُ في أصْلِ الجَحِيمِ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 64]. The idolaters were put to trial by it: Abū Jahl said: "We know zaqqūm only as eating dates with butter — so gulp it down (tazaqqamū)!"

And some of the idolaters said: "Fire consumes trees, so how can trees grow in it?!" For that reason He, exalted be His praise, said: ﴿وَما جَعَلْنا الرُّؤْيا الَّتِي أرَيْناكَ إلا فِتْنَةً لِلنّاسِ والشَّجَرَةَ المَلْعُونَةَ في القُرْآنِ﴾.

If someone says: there is no mention of its being cursed in the Qurʾān, the answer to that is: the disbelievers have been cursed, and they are the ones who eat it. There is another answer as well: the Arabs say of every loathsome and harmful food: "cursed (malʿūn)".

zajjaj:61-61.t: His saying: ﴿إلا إبْلِيسَ قالَ أأسْجُدُ لِمَن خَلَقْتَ طِينًا﴾: the meaning is "to one whom You created as clay". "طِينًا" is accusative in two ways. One of them is tamyīz (specification); the meaning is "to one whom You created from clay". It is also possible that "طِينًا" is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "You brought him into being in the state of his being from clay."

zajjaj:62-62.t:
His saying: ﴿قالَ أرَأيْتَكَ هَذا الَّذِي كَرَّمْتَ عَلَيَّ﴾: "قالَ" comes here without a conjunction because it is in the sense of: "He said: shall I prostrate to one whom I created as clay". [Translator's note: the text reads "خَلَقْتُ" (I created) and "اُسْجُدْ" (prostrate!), as printed; the sense intended is presumably Iblīs's words quoted just before, "shall I prostrate to one whom You created as clay".]

His saying: ﴿أرَأيْتَكَ﴾ is in the meaning of "tell me". The kāf has no grammatical position, because it is mentioned in the address for emphasis. The position of "هَذا" is accusative by "أرَأيْتَكَ", and the answer is omitted; the meaning is: "Tell me about this one whom You have honoured above me: why have You honoured him above me, when You created me from fire and created him from clay?!" This was omitted because there is an indication of it in the speech. The meaning of ﴿لأحْتَنِكَنَّ ذُرِّيَّتَهُ إلا قَلِيلا﴾ is "I shall surely uproot them by leading them astray"; it has also been said: "I shall surely gain mastery over them". What the Arabs say is: "iḥtanakat al-sanatu amwālanā" (the year of drought has uprooted our wealth), when it has destroyed it entirely. The poet said:
؎نَشْكُو إلَيْكَ سَنَةً قَدْ أجْحَفَتْ جَهْدًا عَلى جَهْدٍ بِنا وأضْعَفَتْ
؎واحْتَنَكَتْ أمْوالَنا وجَلَّفَتْ
(We complain to you of a year [of drought] that has ruined us, hardship upon hardship, and weakened us, / and has uprooted our wealth and stripped it bare.)

zajjaj:63-63.t:
His saying: ﴿جَزاءً مَوْفُورًا﴾, i.e. made full (muwaffaran). From it one says: "wafartuhu, afiruhu, fa-huwa mawfūr" (I made it full, so it is full). Zuhayr said:
؎وَمَن يَجْعَلِ المَعْرُوفَ مِن دُونِ عِرْضِهِ يَفِرْهُ ومَن لا يَتَّقِي الشَّتْمَ يُشْتَمِ
(Whoever makes kindness a shield for his honour keeps it whole, and whoever does not guard against insult is insulted.)

zajjaj:64-64.t:
His saying: ﴿واسْتَفْزِزْ مَنِ اسْتَطَعْتَ مِنهم بِصَوْتِكَ﴾ means: "summon them with a summons by which you stir them lightly into answering you". "بِصَوْتِكَ" (with your voice) is explained as: with your call. It has also been said: "with your voice" means with the sounds of singing and pipes.

His saying: ﴿وَأجْلِبْ عَلَيْهِمْ بِخَيْلِكَ ورَجِلِكَ﴾, i.e. "gather against them everything of your stratagems that you are able to". It was said in the exegesis: "his horses and his foot-soldiers" are every horse that runs in disobedience to Allah — it is among the horses of Iblīs — and everyone who walks in disobedience — he is among the foot-soldiers of Iblīs. "Rajil" is the plural of "rājil" (one on foot). "وَرِجالِكَ" is also permissible, in which case it is the plural of "rājil": "rijāl", like "ṣāḥib" and "ṣiḥāb". It is also possible that Iblīs has horses and men on foot.

His saying: ﴿وَشارِكْهم في الأمْوالِ والأوْلادِ﴾, i.e. command them to assign something of their wealth to other than Allah, as Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿فَقالُوا هَذا لِلَّهِ بِزَعْمِهِمْ وهَذا لِشُرَكائِنا﴾ [al-Anʿām: 136], and what they said about the sāʾiba and the baḥīra [camels set free in the name of idols]. The partnership in children is their saying "ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā" and "ʿAbd al-Ḥārith" [as names]. It has also been said that his partnership in children means children of fornication, and this is frequent in the exegesis. Every act of disobedience regarding a child or wealth — Iblīs the accursed is their partner in it.

His saying: ﴿وَعِدْهم وما يَعِدُهُمُ الشَّيْطانُ إلا غُرُورًا﴾.

If someone says: how can it be permissible for Iblīs to be commanded, so that it is said to him: "share with them in wealth and children, and rally against them your horses and your foot-soldiers, and promise them that they will not be resurrected", so that if he does that he is obedient? The answer to that is that the imperative is of two kinds. One of them is to be followed, nothing else. The second: when it has been preceded by a prohibition of what is being commanded, then the meaning of the imperative is threat and intimidation. For you may say: "Do not enter this house!", and when he attempts to enter it you say: "Enter it, if you are a man!" You are not commanding him to enter it; rather you are threatening and intimidating him. This is widely found in the language and in usage. Its like in the Qurʾān is: ﴿اعْمَلُوا ما شِئْتُمْ﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 40], when they have been forbidden to follow their desires and to commit acts of disobedience.

zajjaj:65-65.t: His saying: ﴿إنَّ عِبادِي لَيْسَ لَكَ عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطانٌ﴾, i.e. whoever is sincere, you have no argument against him and no authority. ﴿وَكَفى بِرَبِّكَ وكِيلا﴾, i.e. "Allah suffices as a guardian for His friends, protecting them from accepting anything from Iblīs".

zajjaj:66-66.t: His saying: ﴿رَبُّكُمُ الَّذِي يُزْجِي لَكُمُ الفُلْكَ في البَحْرِ﴾: "يُزْجِي" is explained as "He makes [it] move"; and "qad zajjaytu" means I have pushed the thing forward. This speech is mentioned as conjoined to His saying ﴿كُونُوا حِجارَةً أوْ حَدِيدًا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 50] and His saying ﴿قُلِ الَّذِي فَطَرَكم أوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 51]. So the meaning is that the One who began your creation will resurrect you, and beginning and originating are harder than bringing back. Then He made known to them that the One who was able to subject the ships in the sea — and the ships are like mountains — is able to bring them back. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَلَهُ الجَوارِ المُنْشَآتُ في البَحْرِ كالأعْلامِ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 24], i.e. like mountains. ﴿وَكانَ الإنْسانُ كَفُورًا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 67]: by "man" here the disbelievers specifically are meant.

zajjaj:68-68.t:
His saying: ﴿أوْ يُرْسِلَ عَلَيْكم حاصِبًا﴾: "al-ḥāṣib" is dust in which there is gravel (ḥaṣbāʾ), and "al-ḥaṣbāʾ" is small pebbles.

His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ لا تَجِدُوا لَكم عَلَيْنا بِهِ تَبِيعًا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 69], i.e. you will find no one to pursue Us in protest at what has befallen you, nor anyone to pursue Us in order to turn it away from you.

zajjaj:70-70.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ كَرَّمْنا بَنِي آدَمَ﴾: its interpretation is that Allah, exalted be His praise, favoured them with discernment, with His subjecting to them what is in the heavens and the earth, and with carrying them on land and sea. ﴿وَفَضَّلْناهم عَلى كَثِيرٍ مِمَّنْ خَلَقْنا تَفْضِيلا﴾: He said "over many" and did not say "over all whom We created", because Allah, Majestic and Exalted, has favoured the angels, saying: ﴿وَلا المَلائِكَةُ المُقَرَّبُونَ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 172]; but the son of Adam is favoured over all the other animals, which have no reason and no discernment.

It has come in the exegesis that the excellence of the son of Adam is that he walks upright, while beasts, camels, donkeys and the like walk bent over; and that the son of Adam takes food with his hands and raises it to his mouth, while all the other animals take it with their mouths. What is in the exegesis is part of what the son of Adam has been favoured with; and his excellence lies in the discernment he has been given, the good things he has been provided, and the guidance he has been made to see, together with the countless blessings upon him, very many indeed.

zajjaj:71-71.t: His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ نَدْعُوا كُلَّ أُناسٍ بِإمامِهِمْ﴾ — it is also read "يَوْمَ يَدْعُو", with yāʾ — "كُلَّ أُناسٍ بِإمامِهِمْ": by it is meant the Day of Resurrection. It is accusative on [the implied sense] "remember the day when He will call every people by their imām". It may also be accusative in the sense of "the One who originated you will bring you back on the day when He calls every people by their imām". The meaning of "بِإمامِهِمْ" is: by their religion which they followed as a leader; it has also been said: "by their book", and the meaning is the same. What indicates it is: ﴿فَمَن أُوتِيَ كِتابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ فَأُولَئِكَ يَقْرَءُونَ كِتابَهُمْ﴾, i.e. whoever was upon the truth will be given his book in his right hand; "and they will not be wronged by a fatīl" — the meaning is "they will not be wronged by the amount of a fatīl", and "al-fatīl" is the thin skin in the cleft of the date-stone.

zajjaj:72-72.t:
﴿وَمَن كانَ في هَذِهِ أعْمى﴾, i.e. in this world, ﴿فَهُوَ في الآخِرَةِ أعْمى﴾: this is from blindness of the heart, i.e. he is in the Hereafter more intensely blind. Its interpretation is that if he was blind in this world — when He, Majestic and Exalted, had made [the truth] known to him, given him a way to repentance and allowed him ample time for that until the moment of his death — and he was blind to his right guidance and did not repent, then in the Hereafter he will find no repentance and no escape from what he is in; so he is in the Hereafter more intensely blind ﴿وَأضَلُّ سَبِيلا﴾, i.e. and further astray from the path, because he finds no path to guidance, having been left with [the outcome of] his deeds.

His saying: ﴿وَإنْ كادُوا لَيَفْتِنُونَكَ عَنِ الَّذِي أوْحَيْنا إلَيْكَ لِتَفْتَرِيَ عَلَيْنا غَيْرَهُ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 73]: the meaning of the speech is "they almost tempted you away", and "إنْ" and the lām came in for emphasis. Its interpretation is «that the idolaters said to the Prophet ﷺ: "We will not let you touch the Black Stone until you pay some regard to our gods." So he ﷺ said to himself: "What harm is there to me in doing that, when Allah knows what is in my soul, and I am then able to touch the Stone?!"» This is among what has come in the exegesis.

It has also come in the exegesis «that the idolaters said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Drive away from you the riff-raff of the people and their freedmen, and these whose smell is the smell of sheep" — that was because they used to wear wool — and they said: "Drive these away, if you have been sent to us, so that you may sit with us and we may hear from you." The Prophet ﷺ thought of doing something in that regard by which he might invite them to Islam, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, threatened him concerning it with the severest of threats, and Allah protected him from carrying out what he had resolved upon.» So He said: ﴿وَإذًا لاتَّخَذُوكَ خَلِيلا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 73], i.e. if you had done what they wanted, they would have taken you as a close friend.

zajjaj:74-74.t: ﴿وَلَوْلا أنْ ثَبَّتْناكَ لَقَدْ كِدْتَ تَرْكَنُ إلَيْهِمْ شَيْئًا قَلِيلا﴾ — "تَرْكُنُ", with ḍamma on the kāf, has also been reported; one says "rakana, yarkanu" and "rakana, yarkunu". So Allah threatened him concerning that with the severest of threats, saying: ﴿إذًا لأذَقْناكَ ضِعْفَ الحَياةِ وضِعْفَ المَماتِ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 75]. The meaning is: "had you inclined towards them in that small thing, We would then have made you taste double of life and double of death", i.e. double the punishment of life and double the punishment of death, because you are a prophet, and the punishment would be doubled for you over the punishment of anyone else, were he to commit this offence; as He said: ﴿يا نِساءَ النَّبِيِّ مَن يَأْتِ مِنكُنَّ بِفاحِشَةٍ مُبَيِّنَةٍ يُضاعَفْ لَها العَذابُ ضِعْفَيْنِ﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 30], because the rank of the Prophet, and the rank of his family whom Allah has described, is above the rank of others.

zajjaj:76-76.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإنْ كادُوا لَيَسْتَفِزُّونَكَ مِنَ الأرْضِ لِيُخْرِجُوكَ مِنها﴾: they had nearly expelled the Prophet ﷺ from Mecca, so Allah made known to them that had they done that, they would not have remained after him except a little. It has also been said: "لَيَسْتَفِزُّونَكَ" means "they would kill you".

His saying: ﴿سُنَّةَ مَن قَدْ أرْسَلْنا قَبْلَكَ مِن رُسُلِنا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 77]: "سُنَّةَ" is accusative in the sense of: "We have laid down this practice regarding those of Our messengers whom We sent before you: that when [their peoples] expelled their prophet from among them, or killed him, the punishment did not delay in descending upon them." The departure of the Prophet ﷺ from Mecca was as an emigrant, by the command of Allah.

zajjaj:78-78.t:
His saying: ﴿أقِمِ الصَّلاةَ لِدُلُوكِ الشَّمْسِ إلى غَسَقِ اللَّيْلِ﴾: "the dulūk of the sun" is its declining and inclining at the time of midday; likewise its inclining towards setting is also its dulūk. One says "qad dalakat barāḥi" and "birāḥi", i.e. "it has inclined to decline, so that the onlooker, when he looks at it, needs to break the rays from his eyes with his palm (rāḥa)". The poet said:
؎هَذا مَقامُ قَدَمَيْ رَباحْ لِلشَّمْسِ حَتّى دَلَكَتْ بَراحْ
(This is where the feet of Rabāḥ stood, [facing] the sun, until it declined, [shaded] by the palm.)

His saying: ﴿إلى غَسَقِ اللَّيْلِ﴾, i.e. the darkness of the night. "And the Qurʾān of the dawn", i.e. "and establish the Qurʾān of the dawn". In this place there is a great benefit indicating that the prayer is not valid except with recitation, because His saying "establish the prayer" and "establish the Qurʾān of the dawn" commands us to establish the prayer with recitation, so much so that the prayer was called "Qurʾān" (recitation). So there is no prayer except with recitation.

His saying: ﴿إنَّ قُرْآنَ الفَجْرِ كانَ مَشْهُودًا﴾: it has come in the exegesis that the angels of the night attend the recitation of the dawn, and the angels of the day attend it as well.

zajjaj:79-79.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَتَهَجَّدْ بِهِ نافِلَةً لَكَ﴾: one says "tahajjada al-rajul" (the man kept vigil) when he stays awake, and "hajada" when he sleeps; and "qad hajjadtuhu" when I have put him to sleep. Labīd said:
؎قُلْتُ هَجِّدْنا فَقَدْ طالَ السُّرى وقَدَرْنا إنْ خَنا الدَّهْرُ غَفَلْ
(I said: let us sleep, for the night journey has been long, and we have the power [to do so] if the misfortune of time is heedless.)
And this is a supererogatory act for you (nāfila): an addition for the Prophet ﷺ specifically, not for anyone else, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded him to increase in his worship beyond what all creation has been commanded, because He has favoured him over them. Then He promised him that He would raise him to a praised station (maqām maḥmūd), and what is soundly established by the narrations and reports about the praised station is that it is the intercession.

zajjaj:80-80.t:
His saying: ﴿أدْخِلْنِي مُدْخَلَ صِدْقٍ﴾ — and "مَدْخَلَ صِدْقٍ" — ﴿وَأخْرِجْنِي مُخْرَجَ صِدْقٍ﴾. It has come in the exegesis that "admit me with an admission of truth" is Paradise, and "bring me out with an exit of truth" means: bring me out of Mecca to Medina. It has also come that the admission and exit of truth are his entry into Medina and his exit from Mecca. It has also come that "the admission of truth and the exit of truth" are being admitted into the religion and leaving this world while being upon the truth. And it has also come — and this is good — that it is his entering into the messengership and his coming out from what was obligatory upon him in it ﷺ. All of that is good. Whoever said "مُدْخَلَ", with ḍamma on the mīm, it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of "adkhaltuhu mudkhalan" (I admitted him an admission); and whoever said "مَدْخَلَ صِدْقٍ", it is on [the sense of] "I admitted him, so he entered an entry of truth". The explanation of "مُخْرَجَ" is likewise the same.

His saying: ﴿واجْعَلْ لِي مِن لَدُنْكَ سُلْطانًا نَصِيرًا﴾, i.e. make my help come from You, by empowering me with power and with proof. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, answered his prayer and made known to him that He would protect him from the people, saying: ﴿واللَّهُ يَعْصِمُكَ مِنَ النّاسِ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 67]; and He said: ﴿فَإنَّ حِزْبَ اللَّهِ هُمُ الغالِبُونَ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 56]; and He said: ﴿لِيُظْهِرَهُ عَلى الدِّينِ كُلِّهِ ولَوْ كَرِهَ المُشْرِكُونَ﴾ [al-Tawba: 33].

zajjaj:84-84.t: His saying: ﴿قُلْ كُلٌّ يَعْمَلُ عَلى شاكِلَتِهِ﴾ means: according to his way and his path. What indicates it is: ﴿فَرَبُّكم أعْلَمُ بِمَن هو أهْدى سَبِيلا﴾, i.e. better guided in way. One says "hādhā ṭarīqun dhū shawākil" (this is a road with shawākil), i.e. many roads branch off from it.

zajjaj:85-85.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَسْألُونَكَ عَنِ الرُّوحِ قُلِ الرُّوحُ مِن أمْرِ رَبِّي﴾: «The Jews asked the Prophet ﷺ about the spirit, supposing that he would answer them with something other than what they knew of its explanation. So he informed them that the spirit is of the command of Allah. Then He said:
﴿وَما أُوتِيتُمْ مِنَ العِلْمِ إلا قَلِيلا﴾. So they said to the Prophet ﷺ: "We have been given the Torah, and in it is wisdom, and you have recited: ﴿وَمَن يُؤْتَ الحِكْمَةَ فَقَدْ أُوتِيَ خَيْرًا كَثِيرًا﴾ [al-Baqara: 269]." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known to them that the knowledge of the Torah is little compared with the knowledge of Allah, and said: ﴿وَلَوْ أنَّما في الأرْضِ مِن شَجَرَةٍ أقْلامٌ والبَحْرُ يَمُدُّهُ مِن بَعْدِهِ سَبْعَةُ أبْحُرٍ ما نَفِدَتْ كَلِماتُ اللَّهِ﴾ [Luqmān: 27].»

That is, the wisdom that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, brings would not be exhausted; so the Torah is little in relation to the words of Allah. "Little" and "much" are valid only relatively: a thing is little only when something more than it is known, and likewise it is much in relation to something known that is less than it.

People have differed concerning the interpretation of the spirit. It has been said that the spirit is "Jibrīl", and whoever interpreted it so, his evidence is His saying: ﴿نَـزَلَ بِهِ الرُّوحُ الأمِينُ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 193] ﴿عَلى قَلْبِكَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 194].

It has also been said that the spirit is a creation [in the heavens] in the likeness of the creation of the children of Adam. [Translator's note: the text reads "خَلْقٌ لِخَلْقِ بَنِي آدَمَ في السَّماءِ", literally "a creation for the creation of the children of Adam in the heaven"; it is translated in the sense usually reported for this view.] Some of the exegetes said that by the spirit only the Qurʾān is meant; he said: the evidence for that is His saying: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ أوْحَيْنا إلَيْكَ رُوحًا مِن أمْرِنا ما كُنْتَ تَدْرِي ما الكِتابُ ولا الإيمانُ﴾ [al-Shūrā: 52], and likewise it was said: ﴿الرُّوحُ مِن أمْرِ رَبِّي﴾. The interpretation of naming the Qurʾān "spirit" is that the Qurʾān is the life of hearts, and the life of the soul in the good it comes to with Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

zajjaj:86-86.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَئِنْ شِئْنا لَنَذْهَبَنَّ بِالَّذِي أوْحَيْنا إلَيْكَ﴾, i.e. had We willed, We would have erased it from the hearts and from the books, so that no trace of it would be found; "then you would find for yourself no guardian against Us concerning it".
That is, you would find no one to undertake the return of anything of it.

zajjaj:87-87.t: His saying: ﴿إلا رَحْمَةً مِن رَبِّكَ﴾ is an exception not of the same kind as the first [i.e. a disjoined exception]; the meaning is: but Allah has had mercy on you, so He established that in your heart and in the hearts of the believers. Then, after His argument against them in His saying ﴿قُلْ كُونُوا حِجارَةً أوْ حَدِيدًا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 50], Allah argued against them with the Qurʾān, and made known to them — and they were the pure Arabs, the people of eloquence, masters of composing speech — saying to them: ﴿قُلْ لَئِنِ اجْتَمَعَتِ الإنْسُ والجِنُّ عَلى أنْ يَأْتُوا بِمِثْلِ هَذا القُرْآنِ لا يَأْتُونَ بِمِثْلِهِ ولَوْ كانَ بَعْضُهم لِبَعْضٍ ظَهِيرًا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 88]. Al-ẓahīr is the helper.

zajjaj:90-90.t: His saying: ﴿وَقالُوا لَنْ نُؤْمِنَ لَكَ حَتّى تَفْجُرَ لَنا مِنَ الأرْضِ يَنْبُوعًا﴾: this was their saying after their argument had been cut off, and they had not produced a sūra like the Qurʾān, nor refuted its being a miracle. So they demanded signs to which they had no right, because what he had brought them — the Qurʾān, the splitting of the moon, and that by which he guided them to the Oneness of Allah — was more eloquent and more beyond [human] power than what they demanded. So they said: ﴿حَتّى تَفْجُرَ لَنا مِنَ الأرْضِ يَنْبُوعًا﴾. "Al-yanbūʿ" (spring) is of the pattern "yafʿūl", from "nabaʿa al-shayʾu" (the thing gushed forth).

zajjaj:91-91.t:
His saying: ﴿أوْ تَكُونَ لَكَ جَنَّةٌ مِن نَخِيلٍ وعِنَبٍ فَتُفَجِّرَ الأنْهارَ خِلالَها تَفْجِيرًا﴾ ﴿أوْ تُسْقِطَ السَّماءَ كَما زَعَمْتَ عَلَيْنا كِسَفًا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 92] — and "كِسْفًا". Whoever read "كِسَفًا" made it the plural of "kisfa", which is a piece; and whoever read "كِسْفًا", it is as though he said: or make it fall upon us as a covering layer. Its derivation is from "kasaftu al-shayʾa" when I have covered the thing.

His saying: ﴿أوْ تَأْتِيَ بِاللَّهِ والمَلائِكَةِ قَبِيلا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 92]: concerning "قَبِيلًا" there are two views. It is possible that [it means] you command them [to come] so that we see them face to face; and that "قَبِيلًا" means a guarantor. One says "qabultu bihi, aqbulu, qabālatan" (I stood surety for him), like your saying "kafaltu bihi, akfulu, kafālatan"; and likewise people's saying "qad taqabbala fulānun bi-hādhā", i.e. he has guaranteed it.

zajjaj:93-93.t:
His saying: ﴿أوْ يَكُونَ لَكَ بَيْتٌ مِن زُخْرُفٍ﴾: it has come in the exegesis that its meaning is "a house of gold". The root meaning of "al-zukhruf" in the language, and of "al-zakhrafa", is adornment. The evidence for that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿حَتّى إذا أخَذَتِ الأرْضُ زُخْرُفَها﴾ [Yūnus: 24], i.e. it took on the perfection of its adornment; and "zakhraftu al-shayʾa" when I have perfected its adornment. Nothing adorns, beautifies and embellishes a house like gold, so what they explained it as does not depart from the truth in this.

His saying: ﴿أوْ تَرْقى في السَّماءِ ولَنْ نُؤْمِنَ لِرُقِيِّكَ﴾: one says — of ascending — "raqaytu, arqā, raqyan"; and one says — of what you treat with an amulet-charm — "raqaytu, arqī, ruqyatan wa-raqyan". [Translator's note: the first is usually given as "raqītu, arqā"; the text has "رَقَيْتُ" for both, as printed.]

His saying: ﴿حَتّى تُنَـزِّلَ عَلَيْنا كِتابًا نَقْرَؤُهُ﴾, i.e. until you send down upon us a book that bears witness to your prophethood. So Allah, exalted be His praise, made known that if that were sent down upon them, they would not believe, and said: ﴿وَلَوْ نَـزَّلْنا عَلَيْكَ كِتابًا في قِرْطاسٍ فَلَمَسُوهُ بِأيْدِيهِمْ لَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إنْ هَذا إلا سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 7]. If they claim of what they are incapable of [matching] that it is sorcery, then how can one bring them to insight and make things clear to them with more than what the Prophet ﷺ brought them of the lasting sign, which is the Qurʾān, and of the reports of what they plotted among themselves, and of what he informed them of the reports of past nations — when he had not read a book nor written one with his right hand? He ﷺ informed them, and everything that might occur to the mind indicated his prophethood.

zajjaj:94-94.t:
His saying: ﴿وَما مَنَعَ النّاسَ أنْ يُؤْمِنُوا إذْ جاءَهُمُ الهُدى﴾: the position of "أنْ" is accusative.

His saying: ﴿إلا أنْ قالُوا﴾: the position of "أنْ قالُوا" is nominative; the meaning is: nothing prevented them from believing except their saying: ﴿أبَعَثَ اللَّهُ بَشَرًا رَسُولا﴾. So Allah made known that the fairest towards them and the most effective in conveying to them is a human being like them, and He made known to them that ﴿لَوْ كانَ في الأرْضِ مَلائِكَةٌ يَمْشُونَ مُطْمَئِنِّينَ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 95], i.e. walking about, settled in the earth as their home, ﴿لَنَـزَّلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ السَّماءِ مَلَكًا رَسُولا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 95], because only one of its own kind is sent to a creation.

zajjaj:96-96.t: His saying: ﴿قُلْ كَفى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيدًا بَيْنِي وبَيْنَكُمْ﴾: they said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Who bears witness for you that you are the Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Allah bears witness for me." "كَفى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيدًا": [the genitive "بِاللَّهِ"] is in the position of the nominative; the meaning is "Allah suffices as a witness". "شَهِيدًا" is accusative in two ways: if you wish, as a tamyīz (specification) — "Allah suffices among witnesses"; and if you wish, as a ḥāl (circumstantial) — the meaning being "Allah suffices in the state of bearing witness". [Translator's note: the bracketed words are added for clarity.]

zajjaj:97-97.t: His saying: ﴿كُلَّما خَبَتْ زِدْناهم سَعِيرًا﴾, i.e. whenever it dies down and their skins and flesh are fully burnt, Allah replaces them with others, so that they may taste the punishment.

zajjaj:100-100.t:
His saying: ﴿قُلْ لَوْ أنْتُمْ تَمْلِكُونَ خَزائِنَ رَحْمَةِ رَبِّي﴾: this is an answer to their saying: ﴿لَنْ نُؤْمِنَ لَكَ حَتّى تَفْجُرَ لَنا مِنَ الأرْضِ يَنْبُوعًا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 90]. So Allah, Majestic and Exalted, made known to them that if they owned the treasuries of provisions they would hold back out of avarice and miserliness, and said: ﴿إذًا لأمْسَكْتُمْ خَشْيَةَ الإنْفاقِ وكانَ الإنْسانُ قَتُورًا﴾. By "man" here the disbeliever specifically is meant, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿إنَّ الإنْسانَ لِرَبِّهِ لَكَنُودٌ﴾ [al-ʿĀdiyāt: 6], i.e. ungrateful, ﴿وَإنَّهُ لِحُبِّ الخَيْرِ لَشَدِيدٌ﴾ [al-ʿĀdiyāt: 8], i.e. because of the love of good things — which is wealth — he is miserly.

As for "أنْتُمْ", it is nominative by an implied (muḍmar) verb; the meaning is "say: if you owned", because "لَوْ" is that by which a thing occurs because of the occurrence of another, so only a verb may follow it; and when a noun follows it, the implied verb governs it. Its like in poetry is the saying of al-Mutalammis:
؎فَلَوْ غَيْرُ أخْوالِي أرادُوا نَقِيصَتِي جَعَلْتُ لَهم فَوْقَ العَرانِينِ مِيسَمًا
(Had any but my maternal uncles sought to disparage me, I would have set a brand on their noses.)
The meaning is: had other than my maternal uncles wanted. "Al-qatūr" is the miser.

zajjaj:101-101.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا مُوسى تِسْعَ آياتٍ بَيِّناتٍ﴾: it was said in the exegesis that they are: "the seizing of the people of Pharaoh with years — that is, drought — until their fruits were gone and the livestock of the desert-dwellers among them were gone; among them is Mūsā's bringing out his hand white for the onlookers; among them is his casting down his staff, whereupon it was a manifest serpent, and that it swallowed up the falsehood of the sorcerers; and among them is Allah's sending upon them the flood — we seek refuge in Allah from it — the locusts, the lice, the frogs and the blood". Those are nine signs. It has also been said that the sea is among them; and among his signs is the gushing forth [of water] from the rock, but that has not been narrated in the exegesis [as one of the nine].

His saying: ﴿إنِّي لأظُنُّكَ يا مُوسى مَسْحُورًا﴾
Pharaoh found nothing with which to repel the signs except his own admission that he supposed Mūsā to be bewitched. So Allah made known that Pharaoh had realised clearly that they were signs, and said: ﴿قالَ لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ ما أنْـزَلَ هَؤُلاءِ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 102], meaning the signs, ﴿إلا رَبُّ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ بَصائِرَ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 102]. Some read "لَقَدْ عَلِمْتُ" (I have known), with ḍamma on the tāʾ; and the better in reading is "لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ" (you have known), with fatḥa on the tāʾ, because Pharaoh's knowing that they were signs from Allah is a stronger argument against him. The evidence for that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic, about Pharaoh and his people: ﴿وَجَحَدُوا بِها واسْتَيْقَنَتْها أنْفُسُهم ظُلْمًا وعُلُوًّا﴾ [al-Naml: 14].

His saying: ﴿وَإنِّي لأظُنُّكَ يا فِرْعَوْنُ مَثْبُورًا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 102], i.e. "I think you are doomed to destruction". One says "thubira al-rajul, fa-huwa mathbūr" when he has been destroyed.

zajjaj:103-103.t: His saying: ﴿فَأرادَ أنْ يَسْتَفِزَّهم مِنَ الأرْضِ﴾, i.e. Pharaoh wanted to drive Mūsā and his people out of the land. It is possible that driving them out means removing them from it by killing or by banishment. ﴿فَأغْرَقْناهُ ومَن مَعَهُ جَمِيعًا﴾.

zajjaj:104-104.t: His saying: ﴿جِئْنا بِكم لَفِيفًا﴾, i.e. We will bring you from every tribe. "Al-lafīf" means groups from various tribes.

zajjaj:106-106.t: His saying: ﴿وَقُرْآنًا فَرَقْناهُ﴾ — it is also read "فَرَّقْناهُ", with doubling. "قُرْآنًا" is accusative by an implied (muḍmar) verb; the meaning is: "We have sent you only as a bearer of good tidings and a warner, giving the believers the good tidings of Paradise and warning those who disobey Allah of the Fire; and a Qurʾān which We have divided". Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down the Qurʾān all at once to the lowest heaven, then it was sent down upon the Prophet ﷺ over twenty years; Allah divided it in the revelation so that people might understand it, and He said: ﴿لِتَقْرَأهُ عَلى النّاسِ عَلى مُكْثٍ﴾ — and "makth" too, both forms; and the reading is with ḍamma on the mīm.

zajjaj:107-107.t: His saying: ﴿يَخِرُّونَ لِلأذْقانِ سُجَّدًا﴾: because one who falls down while standing falls on his face, and "al-dhaqan" (the chin) is where the two jaw-bones meet, and it is one of the parts of the face; and as soon as one begins to fall down, the nearest part of his face to the ground is the chin. "سُجَّدًا" is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

zajjaj:108-108.t: His saying: ﴿إنْ كانَ وعْدُ رَبِّنا لَمَفْعُولا﴾ means: the promise of our Lord was nothing but fulfilled. "إنْ" and the lām came in for emphasis.

zajjaj:110-110.t: His saying: ﴿قُلِ ادْعُوا اللَّهَ أوِ ادْعُوا الرَّحْمَنَ أيًّا ما تَدْعُوا﴾: when the Arabs heard mention of al-Raḥmān, they said: "Are you calling us to two — to Allah and to al-Raḥmān?!" The name al-Raḥmān was in the earlier books sent down to the prophets. So Allah made known to them that their calling upon al-Raḥmān and their calling upon Allah come back to one thing, and said: ﴿أيًّا ما تَدْعُوا﴾ — the meaning is: whichever of the names of Allah you call upon — ﴿فَلَهُ الأسْماءُ الحُسْنى﴾. ﴿وَلا تَجْهَرْ بِصَلاتِكَ ولا تُخافِتْ بِها﴾: "al-mukhāfata" is concealing [the voice], and "al-jahr" is raising the voice. When the Prophet ﷺ recited the Qurʾān aloud, the idolaters would revile the Qurʾān, so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, commanded him not to expose the Qurʾān to their reviling, and not to lower his voice in it so much that those of his Companions praying behind him would not hear it. ﴿وابْتَغِ بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ سَبِيلا﴾, i.e. take a path between loudness and lowering.

zajjaj:111-111.t: His saying: ﴿وَقُلِ الحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي لَمْ يَتَّخِذْ ولَدًا ولَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ شَرِيكٌ في المُلْكِ﴾ — to help Him in what He wills — ﴿وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ ولِيٌّ مِنَ الذُّلِّ﴾, i.e. He did not need to seek help from another. ﴿وَكَبِّرْهُ تَكْبِيرًا﴾, i.e. magnify Him with a complete magnification.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Isrāʾ (The Night Journey)
Meccan.
﷽
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿سُبْحانَ الَّذِي أسْرى بِعَبْدِهِ لَيْلا مِنَ المَسْجِدِ الحَرامِ﴾: "سبحان" is accusative (manṣūb) as a maṣdar (verbal noun); the meaning is: "I glorify Allah with a glorification (أسبّح الله تسبيحًا)". The meaning of "سبحان الله" in the language is: declaring Allah free of evil; and likewise what is related from the Prophet ﷺ.

His words: ﴿أسْرى بِعَبْدِهِ لَيْلا﴾: its meaning is: He made His servant travel. One says "أسريتُ" and "سريتُ" when I have travelled by night, and both dialect forms have come in the Quran. Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿واللَّيْلِ إذا يَسْرِ﴾ [al-Fajr: 4]; this is from "سريتُ", and the meaning of "يسري" is: it passes on. Allah, Glory be to Him, took the Prophet ﷺ by night from the Sacred Mosque, which is Mecca — and the whole sanctuary is a mosque. So Allah took him by night, in a single night, from the Sacred Mosque in Mecca to Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis); that is His words, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إلى المَسْجِدِ الأقْصى الَّذِي بارَكْنا حَوْلَهُ﴾. Allah made rivers flow around Jerusalem and made fruits grow; that is the meaning of "بارَكنا حوله" (whose surroundings We have blessed).

﴿لِنُرِيَهُ مِن آياتِنا﴾, that is: to show Muhammad. So Allah showed him that night, of the prophets and their signs, what he told the people of Mecca on the morning after that night. They said to the Prophet ﷺ: "We have camels on the road to Syria; tell us news of them." He told them their news. They said: "Then when will the camels reach us?" He told them that they would arrive on a day he named for them, at sunrise, and that a dusky (أورق) camel would be leading them. They went out on that day, and one said: "Here is the sun, it has risen", and another said: "And here are the camels, they have arrived, led by a dusky camel, as Muhammad ﷺ said." Yet they did not believe after that.

zajjaj:2-2.t: His words: ﴿وَآتَيْنا مُوسى الكِتابَ وجَعَلْناهُ هُدًى لِبَنِي إسْرائِيلَ﴾, that is: We guided them by it to right guidance. ﴿ألا تَتَّخِذُوا مِن دُونِي وكِيلا﴾, that is: do not rely on other than Me, and do not take any lord besides Me.

zajjaj:3-3.t:
His words: ﴿ذُرِّيَّةَ مَن حَمَلْنا مَعَ نُوحٍ﴾: the reading is with "ذرّيّةَ" in the accusative. Some read "ذِرّيّة" with kasra on the dhāl, but the ḍamma is more common. "ذُرّيّة" is of the pattern "فُعْلِيّة", from "الذَّرّ" (tiny ants / seed). It is accusative as a vocative (ʿalā al-nidāʾ) — so most of the views hold — the meaning being: "O descendants of those whom We carried with Noah"; they were reminded of Allah's blessings upon them, in that He saved their forefathers from drowning by their being carried with Noah.

The accusative is also possible in the sense of "that you take not the descendants of those whom We carried with Noah as a trustee (وكيل) besides Me"; then the verb passes over to [two objects]: the descendants and the trustee, as you say "اتخذتُ زيدًا وكيلًا" (I took Zayd as a trustee). And ﴿ألا تَتَّخِذُوا مِن دُونِي وكِيلا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 2] is possible in the sense of: ﴿وَجَعَلْناهُ هُدًى لِبَنِي إسْرائِيلَ ألا تَتَّخِذُوا مِن دُونِي وكِيلا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 2] ﴿ذُرِّيَّةَ مَن حَمَلْنا مَعَ نُوحٍ﴾.

The nominative "ذرّيّةُ" is also grammatically possible, as a badal (substitute) for the wāw [of "تتخذوا"]; the meaning: ﴿ألا تَتَّخِذُوا مِن دُونِي وكِيلا﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 2], that is: "Do not take a trustee besides Me — [you,] the descendants (ذرّيّةُ) …". But do not recite it so unless a sound transmission of it is established, for the reading is a sunna (an established practice) which may not be departed from on the basis of what is permissible in Arabic.

zajjaj:4-4.t:
His words: ﴿وَقَضَيْنا إلى بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ في الكِتابِ﴾: its meaning is: We informed them in the Book and revealed to them. Like that are His words: ﴿وَقَضَيْنا إلَيْهِ ذَلِكَ الأمْرَ أنَّ دابِرَ هَؤُلاءِ مَقْطُوعٌ مُصْبِحِينَ﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 66], whose meaning is: "and We revealed to him".

And His words: ﴿فَقَضاهُنَّ سَبْعَ سَماواتٍ في يَوْمَيْنِ﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 12]: its meaning is: "He created them and completed them". The like of this in poetry is the line:
؎وَعَلَيْهِما مَسْرُودَتانِ قَضاهُما داوُدُ أوْ صَنَعَ السَّوابِغَ تُبَّعُ
(Upon the two of them were two coats of chain mail which David made (قضاهما), or Tubbaʿ fashioned the ample coats.)
Its meaning is: "he made them". The sum of this chapter is that everything that has been made with precise workmanship has been "قُضِي" (accomplished). The judge was called "قاضٍ" only because, when he commands a command, his command is not turned back. So al-qaḍāʾ is the settling of things with precision. The meaning is: "We revealed to them: you will surely cause corruption in the land and you will surely become greatly exalted (لتعلُنّ علوًّا كبيرًا)"; its meaning is: you will surely become arrogant and surely transgress, because of every tyrant it is said: "He has exalted himself (علا) and become arrogant."

zajjaj:5-5.t: His words: ﴿فَإذا جاءَ وعْدُ أُولاهُما﴾: the meaning is: "So when the promise of the first of the two times came". ﴿بَعَثْنا عَلَيْكم عِبادًا لَنا أُولِي بَأْسٍ شَدِيدٍ﴾: it is related that He sent Nebuchadnezzar (Bukhtanaṣṣar) against them. ﴿فَجاسُوا خِلالَ الدِّيارِ﴾, that is: they went about through the dwellings looking to see whether anyone remained whom they had not killed. "الجَوس" is seeking a thing thoroughly.

zajjaj:6-6.t: His words: ﴿ثُمَّ رَدَدْنا لَكُمُ الكَرَّةَ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾, that is: We gave the turn of power back to you. ﴿وَجَعَلْناكم أكْثَرَ نَفِيرًا﴾, that is: We made you more numerous in helpers than them. "نفيرًا" may also be the plural of "نَفْر", just as one says "العَبيد" (slaves), "الكَليب" (dogs), "الضَّئين" (sheep) and "المَعيز" (goats). "نفيرًا" is accusative as a tamyīz (specification).

zajjaj:7-7.t:
His words: ﴿فَإذا جاءَ وعْدُ الآخِرَةِ لِيَسُوءُوا وُجُوهَكُمْ﴾; it is also read "ليسوءَ وجوهكم". The meaning [of the latter] is: "So if the promise of the last came, so that the promise might disgrace your faces." Whoever reads "ليسوؤوا", the meaning is: "so that these people might disgrace your faces." It has also been read "لَيَسوءَنْ وجوهكم", with the light nūn [of emphasis], and its meaning is: "the promise will surely disgrace your faces"; the pause on it is "لَيَسوءَنْ". The best is "لِيسوءَ" without nūn, and "ليسوؤوا". "لِيَسُؤْ وجوهكم" is also grammatically possible, with the verb belonging to the promise, as an imperative (ʿalā al-amr); but do not recite it so. "لِنَسوءَ", with nūn in place of the yāʾ, is also possible.

His words: ﴿وَلِيُتَبِّرُوا ما عَلَوْا تَتْبِيرًا﴾: its meaning is: to destroy. Everything broken, of glass, iron and gold, is called "تِبر". The meaning of "ما علوا" is: "to destroy while they had the upper hand over you".
